6485: This help follows the active program language and the functional version of ECU MEMS Manager.
6600:
This page introduces the purpose of the program and the overall screen layout. The top bar shows the ECU, serial port and communication state, while the side navigation gives access to diagnostics, analysis and documentation.

Use it to choose the correct page and verify the session state without leaving your current work.
6601:
Before communication, install the USB/serial interface driver, connect the cable and verify the COM port assigned by Windows. The ECU must have a stable supply and reliable grounds.

The COM number may change after moving the adapter to another USB socket or changing the driver, so always check the device that is actually present.
6602:
In Windows 11 open Device Manager, then Ports (COM & LPT), to identify the interface. Select the same device in Options.

A K-Line or KKL interface provides the electrical layer; it does not turn MEMS/ROSCO into generic OBD-II. Never connect TTL levels directly to an automotive K-Line without the proper interface.
6603:
Switch the ignition on, select the correct port and click Connect. The communication indicators show link activity and the ECU identification appears when available.

Use Disconnect before intentionally removing the cable. If connection fails, check the port, driver, power supply, grounds and wiring first.
6604:
Overview groups the essential live engine parameters as gauges and short histories: engine speed, temperatures, manifold pressure, throttle, battery, lambda, injection, idle and ignition.

Use this screen for quick monitoring, then confirm suspicious values in All measurements or Automatic diagnostics.
6605:
Adjustments contains the ECU service adjustments that are actually available. Displayed values allow you to observe the effect of a correction without leaving the page.

The hot-idle correction is a user-configured value and must not be replaced by a constant. Interpretation of 7D14-15 remains experimental until fully validated.
6606:
Actuators provides the tests permitted by the ECU: fuel pump, relays, purge, oxygen-sensor heater, fans, stepper motor and other outputs depending on the ECU.

Always secure the vehicle before a test. A command can energize or move a component; do not use a command unless you understand its consequences.
6607:
Errors shows stored faults and anomalies detected live. System status provides an immediate summary.

Read and record the context of a fault before clearing it. The absence of a red warning alone does not rule out a mechanical or electrical fault.
6608:
Automatic diagnostics groups several checks and shows the value, state and interpretation for each one. It can also capture a reference and export a report.

It assists interpretation but does not replace electrical and mechanical checks. Calculations that are not validated must remain clearly identified as such.
6609:
Analysis opens CSV or TXT files recorded by the program. Select channels, display them stacked or overlaid, and use the cursor to inspect a precise instant.

Theme and scale changes only affect the display and never alter the source data.
6610:
All measurements displays parameters in a table with interpreted values and available help. It makes it easy to compare several live quantities.

A sentinel byte or unsupported field must not be shown as a real physical measurement; unknown fields remain identified as unknown.
6611:
ECU / ROSCO exposes the read and session commands used for protocol work: D0, D1, D2, F0 and modes F2 to F5. Responses are shown in hexadecimal.

D3 remains intentionally blocked. No potentially sensitive mode change is sent without an explicit user action.
6612:
All data shows bytes from 7D and 80 frames and, where known, the corresponding decoded value.

This page is for advanced diagnostics and protocol research. A position remains unknown until its meaning has been demonstrated.
6613:
Interactive mode provides access to the commands exposed by the interface and their replies during a session. It allows targeted tests without hiding the experimental nature of some functions.

Undocumented or potentially destructive commands are not normal user functions.
6614:
Recording tools save a session, create a snapshot and let you retrieve captures. Recorded files can later be opened in Analysis.

Use meaningful names for important sessions so they can be compared easily later.
6615:
The MEMS database groups ECU references, vehicle fitments, commands, decodings, capabilities, technical sheets and resources for MEMS 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9.

Information must be accessible without knowing its internal location: added data must be searchable, reachable and displayed in the active language.
6616:
Search accepts a technical term, command, sensor, quantity, connector or natural-language word. What you type remains the query: a suggestion must never replace it automatically.

Queries such as pin, connector, IAT, D0, P0115, battery voltage, K-Line or ROSCO should return all relevant results ranked by proximity.
6617:
Complete XML sheet opens the structured documentation for the selected generation: tables, notes, pinouts and technical information.

The sheet must remain fully vertically scrollable and keep the same structure in all six languages while raw technical data remains unchanged.
6618:
Connector and diagnostic-socket diagrams are part of the database. The preview must show the whole image and Enlarge image opens a view with horizontal and vertical scrolling.

The validated drawings are the MEMS 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9 ECU connectors plus the 3-pin and 16-pin diagnostic sockets; the caption must always match the displayed drawing.
6619:
Options contains the serial port, units, theme, language and available preferences. Supported languages are French, English, Spanish, Italian, Portuguese and German.

Changing language must also update visible help and documentation: no user-facing help text is hard-coded.
6620:
The current scope covers MEMS 1.2, 1.3, 1.6 and 1.9. Available functions depend on the generation, ECU and vehicle.

MEMS 2J and MEMS 3 must not be presented as supported by this database and working protocol.
6621:
For MEMS 1.9 the physical transport uses K-Line while the application protocol remains proprietary MEMS/ROSCO. A KKL interface can provide the electrical layer without making the ECU generic OBD-II.

A J1962-type connector describes the socket form and wiring; it does not by itself define the application protocol.
6622:
When a problem occurs, start from the symptom: no port, wrong port, connection failure, unstable communication, inconsistent value, unsupported file or missing resource.

Check in order: driver and port, power and grounds, cable and interface, then protocol and data interpretation.
6623:
Use a correct power supply, grounds and electrical interface. Actuator tests and some commands can energize or move components.

Undocumented data or a research hypothesis must remain identified as such and must never be presented as established technical fact.
6624:
Help must match the version of the program actually being run. The version number, documented pages and described functions must evolve together.

When a function changes, its chapter and translations must be updated in the same change set so documentation never falls behind the program.
